statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and five representative page templates plus the 404 recovery state.

page.framework: Angular homepage/detail/form templates plus a Next.js Flow template
page.notes: Public AI-experiment directory. Representative coverage excludes authenticated experiences and external product hosts because they are separate origins.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Preference screenshots and computed styles were compared.
Emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce produced zero active animations and exposed multiple explicit reduction rules.
axe contrast and preference CSS were inspected.

checkOutcomes.method: repeat carousel interaction and inspect animations
checkOutcomes.evidence: Repeated carousel changes produced bounded CSS animations and clear active-state updates rather than abrupt swaps.
CSS inspection found four scroll-timeline/animation-timeline rules.
Carousels provide native previous/next buttons, skip affordance and declarative animation; no fighting pointer-only gesture was observed.
Fixed labelled navigation and declarative scroll timelines preserve orientation through the long homepage.
No tooltip, popover, or floating-menu surface appears on the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, popover, or floating-menu surface appears on the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Carousel sections expose previous/next controls, aria-current progress state, category tabs, and a skip-to-next-section link.
Screenshots show a dismissible consent notice with equal Agree and No thanks actions; no unrelated pop-up or interstitial was present.
No site-authored transient overlay or disclosure control appears on the representative paths; the Google consent component is an external platform control with native buttons.
checkOutcomes.reason: No site-authored transient overlay or disclosure control appears on the representative paths; the Google consent component is an external platform control with native buttons.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshots show content-led hero, listing, and detail layouts with restrained navigation chrome.
At 360x800 the layout primitive reports scrollWidth 360, clientWidth 360 and 0 px horizontal overflow; mobile screenshots remain usable.
Distinct desktop/mobile screenshots show carousel, navigation, form and product components reflowing within their available width without overflow.
Focus probe shows visible browser or authored focus indicators on primary controls, and measured primary targets are generally at least 44 px; mobile navigation remains button-operated.
Each first viewport clearly names its experiment or task and presents Try it now, Learn more, Join Waitlist, Express interest, or signup content.
The newsletter flow was exercised with an empty submission.
Invalid form and invalid-route recovery states were exercised.
Lighthouse and a DevTools trace measured load responsiveness and stability.
Mobile layout observation measured CLS 0.00025 and Lighthouse measured 0.
Trace recorded only 17.42 ms TBT with three ~50–60 ms long tasks; Lighthouse TBT was 180 ms.
HAR and DOM media probes measured delivery.
Lighthouse code coverage diagnostics quantified unused JavaScript.
axe and semantic DOM probes examined accessible naming and roles.
axe and Lighthouse measured text contrast.
Landmarks/headings and focus indicators were inspected across templates.
Visual inspection shows comfortable line lengths and unclipped type on detail/listing pages at tested viewports, apart from separately reported contrast.
Viewport permits scaling, mobile layouts reflow without overflow, and principal controls measure around 44–65 px; autoplay hero media is muted/decorative.
Lighthouse errors-in-console audit passed with no entries.
Doctype, charset, media and responsive-image delivery were inspected.
Lighthouse best-practice diagnostics were inspected.
Rendered and raw crawler metadata were compared across routes.
All representative pages expose viewport metadata; navigation uses real href links; robots permits crawling and points to a sitemap.
Representative pages return rendered content, expose canonical URLs, robots allows indexing, sitemap lists routes, and the tested 404 is explicitly noindex.
Every representative page exposes Open Graph metadata and one JSON-LD block matching its visible page type/content.
Transport and main-document response headers were inspected.
No cookies were set before consent; analytics requests carried denied/non-personalised consent signals, although two known analytics origins were contacted.
No permission or authentication surface appears in the covered public discovery and newsletter journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: No permission or authentication surface appears in the covered public discovery and newsletter journeys.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Browser-enforced policy headers were inspected.
Raw HTML retained 80–97% of rendered content across five templates and none was a JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: route screenshots, console and repeated interaction
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative routes and repeated carousel interaction completed without exceptions; controls and state remained present.
The audited surfaces are public marketing/content and server-dependent AI product entry pages; offline completion is not a meaningful core task.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited surfaces are public marketing/content and server-dependent AI product entry pages; offline completion is not a meaningful core task.

checkOutcomes.evidence: An invalid route presents a clear 404 explanation and a Go Home recovery link, with noindex set.
All representative documents declare lang=en, preserve coherent reading order, and reflow at mobile width.
The representative pages expose no dates, currencies, locale-sensitive numbers, durations, or calendars.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative pages expose no dates, currencies, locale-sensitive numbers, durations, or calendars.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative pages expose no events or time values.
checkOutcomes.reason: The representative pages expose no events or time values.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Consent offers equally prominent Agree and No thanks controls; signup terms/data-use text is visible and a Clear form action is present.
The empty newsletter form was submitted and invalid/error announcements inspected.
Identity-field autocomplete metadata was inspected.
No checkout, subscription billing, authentication, or account-management flow exists in the covered site-owned surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: No checkout, subscription billing, authentication, or account-management flow exists in the covered site-owned surfaces.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Rendered and intrinsic image dimensions, formats and srcset were inspected.
HAR and media probes quantified eager background/non-visible transfers.
HAR and tracker probes quantified media and third-party cost.
The audited host is a marketing directory linking to separate experiments, not an agent-facing transactional surface; structured tool exposure is not required for this host.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited host is a marketing directory linking to separate experiments, not an agent-facing transactional surface; structured tool exposure is not required for this host.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The directory and signup pages contain no local inference task where a built-in model or summariser would improve the experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: The directory and signup pages contain no local inference task where a built-in model or summariser would improve the experience.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten full-page scroll cycles, heap size was 25.21 MB versus 23.91 MB baseline (+5.4%); closure count fell slightly and large typed-array populations stayed identical, with no unbounded pattern established.
Baseline retained self size was 23.91 MB for a media-rich Angular directory; runtime JS heap was about 17.3 MB, proportionate to the observed page.
Heap summaries list no Detached* constructor among top retained populations; closure count changed from 23,054 to 22,986 after repetition.

principleOutcomes.reason: All checks were judged not applicable to this marketing/directory host.

paths.description: Homepage and experiment directory: primary discovery journey and shared Angular template.
Experiment detail archetype with app-store and waitlist calls to action.
Distinct science listing template representing themed collection pages.
Primary public form flow, including empty submission and mobile rendering.
Next.js product/tool detail template and app-like marketing surface.

findings.summary: The newsletter template ignores the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The newsletter screenshots are visually unchanged under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark, while the computed probe reports color-scheme: normal and finds no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use preference-driven tokens or light-dark() for page surfaces, text, fields, and browser chrome.

findings.summary: The homepage misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 4.9 s, FCP 4.0 s, Speed Index 15.5 s and performance 0.62; the independent trace measured LCP 3.70 s and FCP 2.97 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise only the initial hero candidate, defer non-visible media, and shorten its critical request chain following the performance guidance.

findings.summary: The homepage eagerly transfers a disproportionate set of hero videos.
findings.evidence: The HAR captured 16.24 MB across 49 requests, including 12.46 MB of media; the DOM probe found four muted autoplay videos, including 5.83 MB, 3.78 MB, 1.89 MB and 0.79 MB hero files.
findings.suggestedFix: Load and prioritise only the visible hero poster/video, lazy-load subsequent slides after intent or idle time, and provide responsive encodes.

findings.summary: Substantial JavaScript is shipped but unused on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 349 KiB unused JavaScript: 229 KiB from the 561 KiB main bundle and about 128 KiB across Google Tag Manager scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split optional experiments and load analytics conditionally after consent or idle time.

findings.summary: Important homepage text has extremely low contrast.
findings.evidence: axe and Lighthouse both report four serious failures at roughly 1.14:1, including “Be the first to experiment”, About copy, and “Stay connected”.
findings.suggestedFix: Change text/surface tokens so normal text reaches 4.5:1 and large text 3:1 in every carousel/background state, then test forced colours.

findings.summary: Carousel progress indicators use prohibited ARIA attributes.
findings.evidence: axe reports aria-label and aria-current on four div elements without a valid role.
findings.suggestedFix: Use actual buttons for interactive progress controls, or remove prohibited ARIA from non-interactive indicators and expose state through a valid pattern.

findings.summary: Landmark and heading structure is inconsistent across major templates.
findings.evidence: axe reports pre-footer content outside landmarks; the homepage has no main landmark and renders several H2s before its H1, while the Flow page exposes no H1 at all.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in main, put a descriptive H1 first on each template, and keep subsequent headings hierarchical.

findings.summary: The main document omits baseline browser security headers.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirms HTTPS but no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP and HSTS first, then nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a minimal Permissions-Policy at the edge.

findings.summary: The newsletter form marks fields required visually but provides no native or announced invalid state.
findings.evidence: First name, last name and email display “*” but required=false; empty requestSubmit produced zero :invalid fields, no role=alert/aria-live message, and no recovery feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply required and meaningful names, validate after interaction, connect field-level messages with aria-describedby, and announce the error summary.

findings.summary: Newsletter identity fields omit autocomplete metadata.
findings.evidence: The form probe reports empty autocomplete values for first name, last name and email.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="given-name", "family-name", and "email", plus stable name attributes.

findings.summary: Many experiment images are oversized and lack responsive candidates.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 8 oversized images and 16 of 20 without srcset; a 4320 px Learn Your Way image displays at 277 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate width-based WebP/AVIF candidates, add sizes/srcset, and cap source dimensions to realistic rendered sizes.

findings.summary: The production JavaScript bundle has no usable source map.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse valid-source-maps reports the large main-M4OSHQNV.js file is missing a source map.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a production source map to an authenticated error-monitoring endpoint or expose a restricted map that DevTools can resolve.

findings.summary: The Science page’s meta description is not present in raw crawler HTML.
findings.evidence: The discoverability primitive found the rendered page description but metaDescriptionPresentInRaw=false, reducing parity for non-JavaScript crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the description in the initial head for the Science route.

taskList.title: Stop eagerly transferring non-visible hero videos and optimise responsive media
Fix homepage colour contrast in every carousel/background state
Make newsletter validation semantic, announced, and recoverable
Repair landmarks, headings, and carousel ARIA semantics
Split unused JavaScript and defer analytics
Respect dark-mode preference on the newsletter template
Add autocomplete tokens to newsletter identity fields
